label: D1 late in episode (trial >= 70) before an a2 choice, after a common a2->S2 trial
explanation: Fires only at D1 (never at GO or D2), and only late in the episode: it is silent before trial ~65, turns on around trials 70-79, and its magnitude grows toward trial 99 (trials 85+ hold ~80% of the activation mass but only ~53% of the activations). Inside that window it needs the previous trial to have been a2 with a common transition to S2 (or no previous trial in the window), and the agent about to choose a2 again. It is almost silent after a1 trials or after rare a2->S1 transitions. It fires after both rewarded and unrewarded previous trials, though 79% of the mass comes after rewarded ones. The value head is always low (<7.1) and the GO policy leans mildly toward a2 (logit diff -4.4 to -1.5). The only future variable is action at D1, which is the agent own upcoming choice and so a legitimate thing for it to compute. The closest observed-only predicate, (phase==D1)&(ep_trial>=70)&(prev_action!=1)&(prev_common!=0), gets dev F1 0.79 (P 0.67, R 0.99); adding the upcoming a2 choice raises it to 0.88 (P 0.82, R 0.96, mass recall 0.98). The late-episode gating suggests it tracks a trial-count or time signal in the hidden state.

issues: Claims check out on dev. The feature fires only at D1, with zero activations at GO or D2. It is silent before trial 60 (trials 60-69 have 117 of 120k steps active), its rate is 0.083 at trials 70-79 and rises to 0.138 at trials 90-99, and trials 90-99 hold 60% of the activation mass. It is near-silent after a1 trials (149 of 423k active), after rare transitions (484 of 253k) and before an a1 choice (1.4% of mass). 79% of the mass comes after a rewarded previous trial.

The predicate's test scores reproduce: P 0.804, R 0.954, F1 0.872, mass recall 0.979. The observed-only version (without the upcoming a2 choice) gets test F1 0.789 (P 0.658, R 0.983), which matches what the explanation reports.

The false positives are mostly one class: the gradual onset. Inside the predicate, precision is 0.39 at ep_trial 70-74, 0.84 at 75-79 and 0.93 at 80+. Raising the threshold to ep_trial >= 73 lifts test F1 from 0.872 to 0.900. This is a threshold refinement of a ramp the explanation already describes, not a new counterexample class.

Second source of false positives: steps where the previous trial is not in the window (prev_action == -1), where precision is 0.66 versus 0.87 when the previous trial is a2. Here the real previous trial is unknown and is probably sometimes a1 or rare. The label's 'after a common a2->S2 trial' really means 'previous trial a2 common, or not in the window', which the explanation does say.

The predicate also passes after unrewarded previous trials, where precision is lower (0.66 versus 0.87 after rewarded). This fits the explanation's statement that 79% of the mass comes after rewarded trials. Calling the late-episode gating a 'trial-count or time signal' is an interpretation, not something these activation checks test.
